clinician.final_diagnosis: chickenpox with bullous impetigo and hypopyon sign due to Staphylococcus aureus superinfection in a child with atopic dermatitis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 3-year-old girl with mild atopic dermatitis presented with high fever and generalized blisters showing hypopyon sign and erosions. VZV infection was confirmed by positive PCR from serum and blisters and positive VZV IgM with negative IgG serology indicating recent infection. Bacterial cultures from skin lesions revealed Staphylococcus aureus superinfection without methicillin resistance. She was diagnosed with chickenpox complicated by bullous impetigo. Following diagnosis, she was hospitalized under isolation and treated with intravenous acyclovir 130 mg TID (10 mg/kg/day) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid 650 mg TID (50 mg/kg/day) for 5 days.
